name: diagnostics_not_responding
description: Investigate a complaint that the customer can't control/reach a device, or nothing happens when they try to control it from NuCore (app, voice, a routine, etc.) -- the NuCore -> device direction. Runs the full mandatory investigation (core services, protocol enabled/connected, then a live status check on the device) in one call, in the correct order, and returns a diagnosis plus a recommended fix when it finds one. Prefer this over manually replaying get_full_system_config/get_core_services_status/send_command yourself for a not-responding complaint -- this can't be skipped or misordered the way a manual sequence can. If the complaint doesn't clearly describe operating a device physically and waiting for NuCore to reflect it, this is the default reading of a vague 'can't communicate with my devices'-style complaint -- use diagnostics_no_status_feedback instead only when the customer explicitly describes a physical/local action not showing up in NuCore.

protocol.description: The device's real protocol family (e.g. "insteon", "zwave", "zigbee", "matter") -- from get_device_family, never guessed from the device's name. Only "insteon" has real automated diagnosis today; other protocols return a plain not-yet-supported result.

device_id.description: The customer-named device, or one representative device if the complaint is general. Required once the system-level checks pass -- omitting it when needed returns an error explaining that.
